title: YFI
story: The throne stands empty above the blue carpet. Below it, four participants lean over proposals spread across a wooden table. The most important seat in this hall is the one nobody has claimed.

On 17 July 2020, Andre Cronje launched YFI, the governance token for Yearn Finance. Its initial 30,000 tokens were distributed through liquidity-based reward pools, with no allocation reserved for the founder or team. Participation in the protocol, rather than a privileged allocation, was the route into that first distribution.

The token also brought decisions. On 19 July, Proposal 0 asked whether future YFI could be minted: the initial supply was already a subject for community debate, not a rule beyond discussion. By 21 July, Cronje had removed himself from the minter set, and a community multisignature wallet held authority over the governance contract controlling who could mint.

Amid DeFi Summer, Yearn made token distribution part of a larger experiment: could a project grow around the people using and governing it? The launch opened that question; proposals, votes and practical responsibilities would shape the answer. Here, the council has work to do while the grand chair waits behind them. The story belongs at the table, not on the throne.

eggs.title: THE EMPTY THRONE
eggs.text: The blue-and-gold seat remains unoccupied, turning the absence of a reserved founder allocation into the scene's central symbol.

eggs.title: FOUR PROPOSALS
eggs.text: Each participant has a parchment marked PROPOSAL, turned towards its reader. The repeated heading makes debate, rather than coronation, the action.

eggs.title: RETURNING FACES
eggs.text: The silver-haired archivist from 030 returns at the rear left, opposite the copper-haired punk from 038. Their familiar profiles link this council to earlier chapters.

eggs.title: BELONGINGS ON THE TABLE
eggs.text: A closed REALCOIN ledger recalls 030. Across its cover lies the punk's CLAIM / 0 ETH + GAS receipt from 038, bringing two earlier stories into the foreground.

claims.limitations: Full token-transparency filing inspected; its submitter identity was not independently authenticated. Etherscan timestamp was accessible in indexed primary-record text; direct page opening failed. Yearn's second-birthday post was embedded with 17 July 2022 date in a secondary page, but original Twitter page could not be opened; it is not a printed citation.

evidence: Historical project documentation calls YFI Yearn's governance token, records 30,000 already distributed, and explicitly permits governance-approved future minting.
Contemporary Proposal 0 (19 July 2020) describes the 30,000 initial supply and reward pools.
guardrails: 30,000 described as initial, never permanent cap.
YFI governance token is not confused with yTokens, which are liquidity receipts.
No legal share-ownership, equal token distribution, one-person-one-vote, returns or price claims.

claims.claim: No reserved founder/team allocation at launch
evidence: YIP-57 (20 January 2021) explicitly records 0% token allocation to the team and discusses how the fair launch left inadequate contributor/treasury funding.
Project governance explainer describes Cronje's launch and early users receiving governance power; canonical brief records no founder allocation.
claims.guardrail: The absence of a reserved allocation does not imply that the founder or contributors could not participate under the applicable pool rules.

claims.claim: Proposal 0 opened future issuance to debate on 19 July
evidence: Contemporary original post dated 19 July 2020 contrasts further minting with a perpetual cap.
YIP-57 later lists Proposal 0's outcome as passed.

claims.claim: By 21 July Cronje was removed from minter set and community multisig held governance-contract authority
evidence: Contemporary announcement dated 21 July 2020 states Cronje removed himself from the minter set, a 6-of-9 community Safe had governance-contract rights, and changing governance was timelocked.
The multisig did not itself expose a direct mint function; it governed minter/control changes.
guardrails: No claim all control was decentralized on launch day.
The four fictional people do not depict the actual nine signers.
